subject: IP carveouts & productization constraints — order form alignment
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: NimbleHealth - procurement <procurement@nimblehealth.com>, NimbleHealth Legal <legal@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Order form: IP & productization scope

Hi Chris / Nimble legal team —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Attached is a first-pass redline of the order form where we tried to capture the items you raised: (1) productization/assignment requests for a small set of outputs, (2) a training opt-out for customer-provided data, and (3) a feedback license scope.

Quick summary of proposed approach in the redline (attached):
- Narrow assignment: non-exclusive assignment for "Customer Productized Outputs" defined by explicit examples and delivery acceptance criteria.
- Training opt-out: toggle to exclude the customer-provided dataset(s) from Redwood model training; includes audit log requirement and a 90-day retention window for complementary telemetry.
- Feedback license: limited, perpetual license for telemetry-only improvements with anonymization and no attribution to customer PII.

Ask: please confirm whether Nimble needs full assignment for all generated outputs or just for a small set they will productize. Also confirm whether the opt-out should apply to all data sent to the API or only tagged data (recommended).

If you confirm priority (assignment vs license) we can surface two pricing options from sales. I cc'd Jordan and Ben to coordinate pricing and legal fallback language.

Attachments: redlines_orderform_v1.docx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Chris Turner <chris.turner@nimblehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbleHealth Legal <legal@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: IP & productization scope

Laura —

Appreciate the redline. A few clarifications from our side:
- We do not need assignment for all outputs. We only need assignment for productized features that are trained and shipped as Nimble-branded capabilities (example: "Clinical Triage Template v1"). For exploratory or transient outputs, a license is fine.
- Training opt-out: Nimble will require that customer-provided PHI/PII is never used for model training; for non-PII, we prefer an opt-in to training rather than opt-out, but can accept an explicit opt-out if accompanied by a written audit and telemetry assurance.
- Feedback license: must exclude any use to re-sell customer-specific prompts or outputs; telemetry may be used for service improvements provided it is aggregated and cannot be reverse-engineered.

Procurement also asked for an estimate of the commercial delta for the assignment option — can you route pricing?

Happy to hop on a 30-min alignment call this week; legal attached a short list of examples they want captured in the order form.

—Chris
Chris Turner
VP, Product — NimbleHealth
chris.turner@nimblehealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: IP & productization scope

Thanks Chris — good clarity. Internal thought / response language for legal:
- Accept limited assignment for "Identified Productized Outputs" (we should define a short exhibit listing examples and acceptance criteria). Assignment only when a separate SOW/SOW schedule is executed that confirms productization and additional consideration.
- For general generated outputs, propose a perpetual, non-exclusive license back to customer (standard).
- Training opt-out: suggest we offer two controls: (A) tagging-based opt-out for specific datasets (recommended) and (B) account-level opt-out for everything, but with an additional fee and SLA carveouts. We should also require a technical attestation and limited audit rights rather than unlimited audits.

Kim — can you draft fallback redline language that (1) adds an exhibit for Identified Productized Outputs and (2) limits training opt-out scope to tagged inputs + customer-provided dataset IDs?

Ben — can you estimate the uplift for assignment + opt-out vs standard license so we can present both options to Nimble?

-Jordan

From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: IP & productization scope

Team —

Draft fallback redlines attached (legal_redlines_v2.pdf). High level:
1) Identified Productized Outputs Exhibit (Exhibit C) — short list of examples + acceptance criteria. Assignment triggers: (a) customer provides written notice of intent to productize and (b) parties execute SOW confirming additional consideration.
2) Training Opt-Out Clause — two-tier approach: account-level opt-out (enterprise add-on with price uplift) or tag-based opt-out (no commercial uplift but limited to specified dataset IDs and endpoints). Include a required "data processing attestation" and an audit window (45 days notice, limited scope).
3) Feedback License — expressly limited to aggregated telemetry for model quality improvements; no use for generating customer-specific outputs; Redwood will not claim ownership of customer data or customer productized outputs beyond the limited assignment described above.

I recommend we avoid blanket assignment language in the main order form. If Nimble wants assignment for a set of outputs, we gate it through Exhibit C + SOW to keep the MSA/order form manageable.

Attachments: legal_redlines_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: IP & productization scope

Quick commercial take —

Two clear paths to present to Nimble:
A) Standard: No assignment, license to use outputs, tag-based training opt-out available at no uplift, feedback license limited to aggregated telemetry. Baseline price X (we'll fill exact numbers in HS record).
B) Enterprise Productization Option: Assignment for items listed in Exhibit C, account-level training opt-out, extended audit rights for scope-limited assessments, and an SLA/operational support package. This carries a material uplift (recommend +25–35% ARR or a one-time fee for assignment rights depending on how many named outputs).

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks all — good progress. Proposed next steps:
1) Nimble to confirm whether assignment is required for any named productized outputs and, if so, share 1–2 examples and expected acceptance criteria (we can draft Exhibit C).
2) Redwood to produce a short decision matrix (Standard vs Enterprise) with pricing impacts and sample contract language (Jordan/Kim/Ben to own).
3) Schedule a 30-min alignment call this Thurs or Fri to review the exhibit draft and the pricing matrix.

Chris — can you confirm availability and send the sample output examples? If Nimble prefers an account-level opt-out that will require confirmation for commercial uplift.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and attach the legal redlines + pricing matrix.
